subject.title: fix: active-memory recall fails with billing rejections on subscription-only Claude CLI setups

question: Should subscription-auth CLI execution become a generic embedded-run dispatch mode, or be integrated into the canonical runtime-plan/provider ownership seam?
rationale: The choice controls credential routing, MCP authorization, transcript ownership, and lifecycle backpressure across future helper callers, so the patch should not define the permanent boundary without owner intent.

options.title: Integrate canonical runtime planning
options.body: Move the CLI decision behind session and lane admission and let the prepared runtime/provider plan own credential and backend selection.

options.title: Keep the opt-in dispatch seam
options.body: Retain the new parameter but explicitly approve its lifecycle differences and add equivalent lane, session-target, and upgrade coverage.

options.title: Scope the fix to Active Memory
options.body: Keep core unchanged and expose a narrower plugin runtime helper if maintainers do not want generic embedded-run CLI dispatch.

recommendation.title: Integrate canonical runtime planning
recommendation.body: Move the CLI decision behind session and lane admission and let the prepared runtime/provider plan own credential and backend selection.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced Active Memory and are the strongest available history-backed owner for deciding its helper-run contract, with core runtime and security review still needed.
